title: Flow Gate Reservoirs: region-aware soft-drop and priority allocations
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description:
Problem: During cross-region failovers and transient overloads we need a deterministic, observable mechanism to favor critical tenants and routes while preserving capacity for fast recovery. Existing lane-based shedding is brittle when regional capacity diverges and when traffic mixes low-throughput long-running requests with high-throughput short ones.

Proposed solution summary: Implement a "Flow Gate Reservoir" subsystem that combines: (1) token-reservoirs per service-class and per-region for hard reservation, (2) an elastic overflow lane with probabilistic soft-drop ("soft-drop" means attempt response morphing or partial responses before hard reject), and (3) a small fast-path admission hint layer to prioritize requests that are latency-sensitive. The system integrates with the regional orchestrator and circuit-breaker signals to shift tokens between reservoirs during failover windows.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic prioritization across regions so critical SLAs remain met during failures.
- Reduce hard rejects by increasing measurable soft-degradation events (response morphing, trimmed outputs, cached-kv fallback).
- Make decisions traceable to SLOs and explainable in Console (why a request got soft-dropped).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement model-level quantization or per-model kernel selection. It focuses on admission and staged degradation only.
acceptance_criteria: Flow Gate Reservoirs implemented in runtime control plane and enabled behind a feature flag.
Per-region reservoirs track token occupancy and expose metrics: reserved_tokens, used_tokens, soft_drop_rate, hard_reject_rate per service-class.
System can move up to 20% of reservoir tokens between regions during a defined failover window under operator control.
Soft-drop outcomes (morphed/partial/cached responses) appear in Console with an audit trail indicating policy and fallback used.
End-to-end tests that simulate regional capacity divergence show preserved P95 latency for 'critical' lane by sacrificing non-critical lane throughput in tests.
Canary rollout demonstrates <0.5% increase in severe errors and measurable decrease in absolute hard rejects vs baseline under identical load spike.
Playbook added to runbook for operator toggle, emergency reclaim, and rollback without data-plane restarts.
tasks: Design API: reservoir config CRD and per-tenant service-class mappings (owner: Liam).
Runtime: implement token-reservoir counters and atomic borrow/return ops with Redis-backed persistent counters (owner: SRE team).
Admission: add fast-path hint evaluation for latency-sensitive routes and integrate with reservoir check (owner: runtime team).
Soft-degradation handlers: implement response morphers (trim, cached-kv fallback, short-suffix placeholder) and standardize response envelope for Console to display (owner: inference-team).
Orchestration: region-token-migration controller with operator workflow and safety checks (owner: platform team).
Telemetry: add metrics, traces, and logs; ensure Console can query by request_id for why soft-drop occurred (owner: observability).
E2E tests: integrate with chaos-testing harness to simulate AZ/regional outages and verify fallback behavior (owner: test-engineering).
Documentation: PRD + operator playbook + console docs (owner: PM: Sofia Martinez).
decision_log: 2025-03-11: Chose token-reservoir abstraction over pure priority queues to allow elastic token transfers during failovers — provides clearer budgeting for reserved capacity.
2025-03-13: Soft-drop preferred to immediate hard rejects; agreed to implement at-most-one soft-degrade attempt then hard reject to avoid degrading downstream reliability.
2025-03-16: Selected Redis for persistent counters to support cross-process atomicity and simple drift correction. We will evaluate switching to tenant-level local caching for perf in a follow-up.
2025-03-18: Decided soft-degradation modes will be ordered: cached-kv fallback -> trimmed-generation -> synth-placeholder. Each mode annotated in telemetry for user debugging.
2025-03-20: Operator-controlled token migration limit set to 20% per 10-minute window to prevent aggressive steal from healthy regions during transient spikes.
rollout_plan: 1. Merge behind feature-flag disabled by default.
2. Canary in staging with synthetic traffic that mixes critical/non-critical lanes (3 days).
3. Enable for small subset of production tenants (5% traffic) and monitor metrics for 48 hours.
4. Gradual ramp to 50% over one week if soft-drop rates are within thresholds and hard rejects decrease.
5. Full enable across regions with operator-run token migration test during low-traffic window.
